candidates.name: catalog-fenced-examples
candidates.title: Exclude fenced Markdown examples from the MCP catalog
candidates.body:
## Problem

The Markdown scanner currently treats entry-shaped lines and category headings inside fenced examples as live catalog content. A documentation example can therefore create a phantom server or change the category of a real entry after the code block.

## Change

Track backtick and tilde fences before scanning headings or entries. Close a fence only with the same marker, sufficient length, and whitespace-only suffix. Preserve source line numbers, ignore an unclosed block through EOF, and keep invalid fence-like lines from suppressing real entries. The tests cover indented fences, longer closing markers, false closers, CRLF input, and categories inside examples. Fence handling follows the [CommonMark rules](https://spec.commonmark.org/0.31.2/#fenced-code-blocks).

## Validation

Tested the exact independent commit on Node.js 20 and 24. With unchanged production code, the focused suite has **12 failures and 15 passes**. With this fix, the complete suite has **107 passes**, with no failures or skips. Catalog generation, profile generation, TypeScript checking, and the package build also pass on both runtimes.

- [Node.js 20 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43855460282/job/133258448423)
- [Node.js 24 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43855460282/job/133258448485)

candidates.name: catalog-large-blame-output
candidates.title: Keep source timestamps for large catalog category files
candidates.body:
## Problem

The synchronous Git invocation uses Node's default 1 MiB captured-output limit. Once line-porcelain blame output exceeds that limit, the command throws and the optional-metadata catch silently drops every timestamp and source PR number for the category.

## Change

Set an explicit bounded 64 MiB capture limit. Add an integration test that creates a real temporary Git repository with 2,048 entries, verifies that blame output exceeds 1 MiB, and checks every resulting timestamp and PR number. Keep the existing behavior for builds outside Git checkouts.

## Validation

Tested the exact independent commit on Node.js 20 and 24. With unchanged production code, the focused suite has **1 failure and 2 passes**. With this fix, the complete suite has **94 passes**, with no failures or skips. Catalog generation, profile generation, TypeScript checking, and the package build also pass on both runtimes.

- [Node.js 20 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43855460282/job/133258448336)
- [Node.js 24 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43855460282/job/133258448222)

The three largest current category files retain identical source coverage before and after the change. At the tested base, the largest produces **944,754 bytes** of blame output and **1,593 source lines**, so this addresses growth past the buffer boundary; it does not claim that this current file has already lost metadata.

candidates.name: python-pip-setup-commands
candidates.title: Skip Python pip setup steps when generating MCP launch configs
candidates.body:
## Problem

A metadata sequence containing `python -m pip install ...` followed by the actual server command currently selects the installation step as the MCP process. The generated client configuration installs dependencies and exits instead of starting the server. The existing AI Memory Book catalog entry reproduces this with its install-then-run metadata.

## Change

Treat `python`/`python3 -m pip` and `-m pip.__main__` as setup commands, so the existing selection logic continues to the next runnable command. Preserve runnable modules such as `pip_server` and `pipx`. If no launch command remains, keep the existing remote-endpoint or placeholder fallback.

The regression tests cover all four installer forms, subsequent launch selection, installer-only metadata, remote fallback, legitimate Python modules, and the real catalog entry across all four client formats.

## Validation

Tested the exact independent commit on Node.js 20, 22, and 24. With unchanged production code, the focused suite has **13 failures and 15 passes**. With this fix, the complete suite has **107 passes**, with no failures or skips. Catalog generation, profile generation, TypeScript checking, and the package build also pass on all three runtimes.

- [Node.js 20 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43854100905/job/133253820040)
- [Node.js 22 and 24 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43853420025)

candidates.name: quoted-launch-arguments
candidates.title: Preserve quoted MCP launch arguments and reject incomplete commands
candidates.body:
## Problem

The launch-command tokenizer drops empty quoted arguments and removes backslashes that are literal inside single quotes or before ordinary characters in double quotes. This changes the argv passed to the MCP server: an empty option value can consume the next option, and a quoted path can point to the wrong file.

The raw shell-operator check also rejects quoted dependency constraints. The existing Trading Research Agents entry uses `uvx --with "mcp>=2,<3" trading-research-agents mcp serve`, but its configuration currently falls back to a placeholder.

## Change

Track whether an argument has started independently of its length, apply quote-aware escaping, preserve escaped trailing spaces, and handle line continuations. Reject incomplete quotes and dangling escapes.

Check shell operators during tokenization so quoted or escaped punctuation remains literal while unquoted `;`, `&`, `|`, `<`, and `>` are rejected. The regression cases cover all four clients, unsafe-operator controls, and configuration generation from the existing Trading Research Agents catalog entry.

## Validation

Tested the exact branch head on Node.js 20 and 24. With unchanged production code, the focused suite has **19 failures and 24 passes**. With this fix, the complete suite has **122 passes**, with no failures or skips. Catalog generation, profile generation, TypeScript checking, and the package build also pass on both runtimes.

- [Node.js 20 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43859714230/job/133273022788)
- [Node.js 24 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43859714230/job/133273022673)

candidates.name: catalog-description-punctuation
candidates.title: Preserve punctuation inside whitespace-separated catalog descriptions
candidates.body:
## Problem

Whitespace-separated descriptions are supported, but their first internal colon or spaced dash is mistaken for the entry separator. For example, `Fetch https://example.com/api for live results.` loses `Fetch https`, and `Runs at 12:30 UTC.` loses `Runs at 12`. This corrupts both profile text and the text available to search.

## Change

Recognize the initial separator only before textual content starts. Preserve punctuation within fallback descriptions while retaining leading status icons, metadata links, and the existing colon/hyphen/em-dash/en-dash forms. Add regressions for URLs, times, ordinary and Unicode descriptions, plus initial-separator controls.

## Validation

Tested the exact independent commit on Node.js 20 and 24. With unchanged production code, the focused suite has **7 failures and 17 passes**. With this fix, the complete suite has **104 passes**, with no failures or skips. Catalog generation, profile generation, TypeScript checking, and the package build also pass on both runtimes.

- [Node.js 20 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43855460282/job/133258448321)
- [Node.js 24 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43855460282/job/133258448526)

candidates.name: registry-invalid-request-target
candidates.title: Reject malformed HTTP targets without terminating the registry API
candidates.body:
## Problem

The HTTP handler constructs a `URL` before entering its error handler. A malformed request target such as `//[` or `http://localhost:bad` throws from that constructor, escapes the async request callback, and terminates the API process under Node's default unhandled-rejection behavior. The failed request can therefore interrupt unrelated clients.

## Change

Catch URL-construction errors at the request boundary and return the existing JSON error format with status 400. Route dispatch remains unchanged for valid targets.

The regressions launch the real API in an isolated child process, send four malformed targets over HTTP, check the 400 response, and then check `/health` in the **same process**. This exercises process survival without changing global rejection handling or relying on a mocked URL parser.

## Validation

Tested the exact independent commit on Node.js 20, 22, and 24. All **4** new HTTP regressions fail against unchanged production code. With this fix, the complete suite has **96 passes**, with no failures or skips. Catalog generation, profile generation, TypeScript checking, and the package build also pass on all three runtimes.

- [Node.js 20 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43854100905/job/133253819541)
- [Node.js 22 and 24 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43853420025)

candidates.name: registry-client-own-aliases
candidates.title: Reject inherited property names as MCP client aliases
candidates.body:
## Problem

The install-config endpoint looks up the requested client on a normal object without checking ownership. Names such as `constructor` and `__proto__` therefore resolve to inherited values and incorrectly receive a successful configuration response instead of the documented unsupported-client error. Case variants also reach the same path after lowercasing.

## Change

Require an own property of `CLIENT_ALIASES` before returning the alias. Keep the existing case-insensitive aliases and the existing 400/no-store error response. Add HTTP regressions for inherited names, mixed-case variants, and an ordinary unsupported name.

## Validation

Tested the exact independent commit on Node.js 20, 22, and 24. With unchanged production code, the focused suite has **4 failures and 17 passes**. With this fix, the complete suite has **97 passes**, with no failures or skips. Catalog generation, profile generation, TypeScript checking, and the package build also pass on all three runtimes.

- [Node.js 20 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43854100905/job/133253819975)
- [Node.js 22 and 24 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43853420025)

candidates.name: independent-placeholder-configs
candidates.title: Keep placeholder configurations independent across callers
candidates.body:
## Problem

Every fallback installation configuration returns the same module-level placeholder object. Mutating a returned command, argument list, or nested configuration can therefore change configurations subsequently generated for another server or client.

## Change

Create a fresh placeholder object and argument array for each call. Regression tests cover independent results across all four clients and mutations of one result followed by another generation.

## Validation

On both Node.js 20 and 24, the unchanged implementation produces **5 failures and 13 passes** in the focused suite. The fix passes the complete **97-test suite**, catalog generation, profile generation, TypeScript checking, and package builds.

- [Node.js 20 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43859062490/job/133270783371)
- [Node.js 24 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43859062490/job/133270783816)

candidates.name: catalog-build-error-status
candidates.title: Fail the catalog build when validation reports errors
candidates.body:
## Problem

The catalog CLI writes validation errors to its diagnostic file but still exits successfully. A build or deployment can therefore continue after duplicate URLs, malformed entries, or missing documentation mirrors have invalidated the catalog.

## Change

Set a failing process exit code when catalog validation reports errors, after writing the catalog and diagnostics. Valid builds continue to exit successfully.

The regression tests invoke the actual CLI in temporary workspaces and check exit status together with the generated diagnostic files for three error cases and two valid controls.

## Validation

On both Node.js 20 and 24, the unchanged CLI produces **3 failures and 2 passes** in the focused suite. The fix passes the complete **97-test suite**, catalog generation, profile generation, TypeScript checking, and package builds. The repository's real catalog still builds with **9,846 entries and zero errors**.

- [Node.js 20 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43859714230/job/133273022861)
- [Node.js 24 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43859714230/job/133273022244)

candidates.name: catalog-inline-code-commands
candidates.title: Extract installation commands from complete inline-code spans
candidates.body:
## Problem

The installation-command expression can start at a closing backtick and consume prose until the next opening backtick. A description such as two code spans separated by “requires npm and Git” can consequently publish that prose as an installation command. Substrings such as `pipeline_summary` are also mistaken for `pip` commands.

## Change

Extract complete inline-code spans first, matching the opening and closing backtick runs, then recognize supported command words within each span. Preserve actual setup commands and the existing pip3, pipx, and pnpm forms.

## Validation

On Node.js 20 and 24, the unchanged implementation produces **6 failures and 17 passes** in the focused suite. The fix passes the full **103-test suite**, catalog and profile generation, TypeScript checking, and package builds. The real catalog contains **9,846 entries and zero build errors**.

- [Node.js 20 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43859544516/job/133272423391)
- [Node.js 24 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43859544516/job/133272422875)

candidates.name: catalog-repository-endpoints
candidates.title: Avoid inferring GitHub repository pages as remote MCP endpoints
candidates.body:
## Problem

A GitHub repository page whose path contains `mcp` or ends in `/sse` is inferred to be a remote MCP endpoint. Installation configuration can then send clients to a repository HTML page. This affects existing entries including Learn MCP Server, Chatpack, and Semgrep MCP.

## Change

Exclude GitHub repository-page URLs from endpoint inference. Keep explicit endpoint metadata authoritative, and preserve real endpoint inference for other hosts, including `gitlab.com/api/v4/mcp` and GitHub Pages.

Tests cover GitHub URL variants, valid remote endpoint controls, metadata precedence, and the three affected catalog entries. An explicitly configured endpoint is intentionally governed by its metadata.

## Validation

On Node.js 20 and 24, unchanged production code produces **7 failures and 17 passes** in the focused suite. The fix passes the complete **104-test suite**, catalog and profile generation, TypeScript checking, and package builds. The real catalog contains **9,846 entries and zero build errors**.

- [Node.js 20 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43859544516/job/133272423326)
- [Node.js 24 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43859544516/job/133272423359)

candidates.name: catalog-gnu-license-identifiers
candidates.title: Preserve GNU license version-choice suffixes in catalog metadata
candidates.body:
## Problem

GNU license inference truncates version-choice suffixes: for example, a description stating `GPL-3.0-only` becomes `GPL-3.0`. This discards part of the stated identifier in the catalog and generated profiles. Eight existing entries are affected by this inference.

## Change

Preserve `-only` and `-or-later` suffixes for the supported GNU license versions. Keep existing unsuffixed identifiers and explicit metadata precedence unchanged. Regression coverage includes the actual Folio entry and suffix variants.

The distinction is part of the SPDX identifiers, for example [GPL-3.0-only](https://spdx.org/licenses/GPL-3.0-only.html) and [GPL-3.0-or-later](https://spdx.org/licenses/GPL-3.0-or-later.html). This change preserves the identifier stated in the description.

## Validation

On Node.js 20 and 24, unchanged production code produces **8 failures and 18 passes** in the focused suite. The fix passes the full **106-test suite**, catalog and profile generation, TypeScript checking, and package builds. The real catalog contains **9,846 entries and zero build errors**.

- [Node.js 20 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43859544516/job/133272423333)
- [Node.js 24 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43859544516/job/133272423290)

candidates.name: incremental-profile-writes
candidates.title: Preserve unchanged profile files during catalog rebuilds
candidates.body:
## Problem

Every profile build deletes and rewrites every JSON profile, even when the catalog has not changed. This performs avoidable filesystem work and changes modification times for unchanged profiles.

## Change

Compare each expected profile's serialized contents with the existing file and write only changed or new profiles. Remove stale JSON profiles after processing the expected files. Preserve unrelated files.

Regression tests check unchanged modification times, one changed profile alongside an unchanged one, stale-profile removal, unrelated-file preservation, and an empty catalog.

## Validation

On Node.js 20 and 24, unchanged production code produces **2 failures and 3 passes** in the focused suite. The fix passes the complete **95-test suite**, catalog and profile generation, TypeScript checking, and package builds.

A Node.js 20 benchmark rebuilds the repository's **9,846-profile catalog** three times with unchanged input:

| Measurement | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median profile-writing time | 547.54 ms | 225.83 ms |
| JSON profiles rewritten per rebuild | 9,846 | 0 |

The output bytes have the same SHA-256 digest before and after. These measurements cover repeated unchanged builds on the validation runner; they do not claim a speedup for the initial build.

- [Node.js 20 tests and benchmark](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43859544516/job/133272423293)
- [Node.js 24 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43859544516/job/133272423460)

candidates.name: duplicate-sidecar-ids
candidates.title: Reject conflicting metadata sidecars instead of silently overwriting them
candidates.body:
## Problem

Two metadata sidecars can resolve to the same server ID, through explicit IDs or a filename-derived fallback. The loader silently lets the later filename overwrite the earlier metadata, so renaming a file can change the published server configuration.

## Change

Reject duplicate IDs and include both source paths in the error. Distinct explicit and filename-derived IDs keep their existing behavior; unrelated non-JSON files are ignored.

## Validation

The unchanged loader produces **3 failures and 4 passes** in the focused suite. On Node.js 20 and 24, the fix passes the full **96-test suite**, real catalog generation, profile generation, TypeScript checking, and package builds. The existing 9,846-entry catalog has no conflicting sidecars and still builds with zero errors.

- [Node.js 20 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43862791585/job/133283602083)
- [Node.js 24 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43862791585/job/133283601902)

candidates.name: decoded-registry-paths
candidates.title: Resolve encoded server identifiers and reject malformed URL escapes
candidates.body:
## Problem

Registry routes pass percent-encoded path segments directly to server lookup. Encoded IDs such as `postgres%2Dmcp`, names containing spaces, and encoded `owner%2Frepository` aliases fail to resolve even though the decoded identifier is supported. Malformed escapes are also treated as missing servers.

## Change

Decode each path segment after splitting the pathname, preserving an encoded slash within one server identifier. Return a JSON 400 response for malformed escapes. Decode only once.

Tests compare actual HTTP responses for three encoded identifier forms across JSON profiles, HTML profiles, both badge routes, and installation configuration. They also cover malformed escapes, subsequent health requests, unresolved aliases, and double-encoded input.

## Validation

The unchanged server produces **18 failures and 18 passes** in the focused suite. On Node.js 20 and 24, the fix passes the full **112-test suite**, catalog and profile generation, TypeScript checking, and package builds.

- [Node.js 20 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43862791585/job/133283601365)
- [Node.js 24 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43862791585/job/133283601922)

candidates.name: registry-cli-special-paths
candidates.title: Start the registry API from paths containing URL punctuation
candidates.body:
## Problem

The API entrypoint constructs a file URL by concatenating `file://` with a filesystem path. A checkout path containing `#`, `?`, or literal percent escapes is interpreted as URL syntax, so the direct-run comparison fails and the production API exits without starting.

## Change

Convert `import.meta.url` to a filesystem path with `fileURLToPath` before comparing it to the resolved entrypoint path.

Regression tests compile the project and launch the actual production Node entrypoint from temporary directories containing those characters, plus ordinary and space-containing controls. The child process must report a listening API and loaded catalog before cleanup.

## Validation

The unchanged entrypoint produces **3 failures and 2 passes** in the focused suite. On Node.js 20 and 24, the fix passes the full **97-test suite**, catalog and profile generation, TypeScript checking, and package builds.

- [Node.js 20 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43863499933/job/133286044795)
- [Node.js 24 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43863499933/job/133286045158)

candidates.name: balanced-catalog-link-destinations
candidates.title: Preserve balanced and escaped parentheses in catalog URLs
candidates.body:
## Problem

The Markdown entry expression stops a link destination at the first closing parenthesis. Valid URLs with balanced parentheses are truncated, and escaped parentheses remain incorrect. The shortened URL then changes the catalog link and its stable identifier.

## Change

Scan the destination while tracking nested parentheses and escaped delimiters. Preserve the complete URL and reject unfinished destinations. Existing descriptions and source line numbers keep their current handling.

Tests cover nested pairs, query values, escaped opening and closing parentheses, encoded-parenthesis controls, incomplete destinations, and the resulting catalog URL and identifier. Balanced and escaped parentheses are valid link destinations under the [CommonMark link rules](https://spec.commonmark.org/0.31.2/#link-destination).

## Validation

The unchanged parser produces **9 failures and 13 passes** in the focused suite. On Node.js 20 and 24, the fix passes the full **102-test suite**, catalog and profile generation, TypeScript checking, and package builds. The real catalog still builds with 9,846 entries and zero errors.

- [Node.js 20 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43863220510/job/133285082383)
- [Node.js 24 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43863220510/job/133285082428)

candidates.name: catalog-grouped-tool-counts
candidates.title: Parse complete grouped tool counts without truncating numeric values
candidates.body:
## Problem

Tool-count inference accepts a suffix of a numeric expression: `1,234 tools` becomes 234, and `1.5 tools` becomes 5. Oversized integers also lose precision when converted to JavaScript numbers.

## Change

Recognize complete nonnegative integers, including correctly grouped thousands separators. Reject decimal, malformed grouping, signed, range, and unsafe-integer values instead of publishing a misleading count. Preserve ordinary and zero counts, singular/plural forms, and explicit metadata precedence.

## Validation

The unchanged implementation produces **13 failures and 18 passes** in the focused suite. On Node.js 20 and 24, the fix passes the complete **111-test suite**, catalog and profile generation, TypeScript checking, and package builds. The real catalog still builds with 9,846 entries and zero errors.

- [Node.js 20 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43863220510/job/133285082476)
- [Node.js 24 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43863220510/job/133285082440)

candidates.name: registry-head-method
candidates.title: Support HEAD requests and advertise allowed registry methods
candidates.body:
## Problem

Every HEAD request currently returns 405, including requests for working health, search, profile, badge, and installation endpoints. Method-rejection responses also omit the `Allow` header.

## Change

Route HEAD through the same handlers as GET; Node suppresses the response body. Advertise GET, HEAD, and OPTIONS consistently in CORS responses and the `Allow` header for OPTIONS and 405 responses. Document the supported behavior.

The HTTP integration tests compare status and representation headers for 15 routes, including error responses, and verify empty HEAD bodies, preflight behavior, and rejected methods. These changes follow [HTTP method and Allow semantics](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-10.2.1).

## Validation

The unchanged server produces **20 failures and 16 passes** in the focused suite. On Node.js 20 and 24, the fix passes the full **112-test suite**, catalog and profile generation, TypeScript checking, and package builds.

- [Node.js 20 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43863220510/job/133285082443)
- [Node.js 24 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43863220510/job/133285082143)

candidates.name: bounded-search-ranking
candidates.title: Keep only the requested best matches while ranking catalog searches
candidates.body:
## Problem

Catalog search scores and sorts every matching entry before returning at most 100 results. Common queries and unfiltered listings therefore retain and sort thousands of entries that cannot appear in the response.

## Change

Keep a sorted result list bounded by the normalized request limit. Skip candidates that cannot improve the current results and use binary insertion for candidates that can. Preserve scoring, filtering, category/name ordering, and original order for exact ties.

## Validation

The focused ordering suite passes all **24 tests** on the unchanged and modified implementations. It checks result limits, ranked and unfiltered ordering, exact ties, filters, and unchanged input order. The complete **106-test suite**, catalog/profile generation, TypeScript checking, and package builds pass on Node.js 20 and 24.

A Node.js 20 benchmark uses the real **9,846-entry catalog**, five query forms, and limits 1, 5, 25, and 100. All 20 result sets have exactly the same serialized summaries before and after. Each measurement uses five warmup calls, then five samples of ten calls.

For the default limit of 25:

| Query | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Empty query | 3.058 ms | 0.230 ms |
| mcp | 6.890 ms | 3.332 ms |
| search | 5.054 ms | 3.987 ms |
| postgres | 4.016 ms | 3.590 ms |
| search mcp | 8.936 ms | 5.365 ms |

These are in-process search times on the validation runner, excluding network latency.

- [Node.js 20 tests and full benchmark](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43863688716/job/133286688010)
- [Node.js 24 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/awesome-mcp-servers-tensorblock/actions/runs/43863688716/job/133286687376)
